sentences.text:
THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S 482 OF CR.PC PRAYING TO  QUASH THE FIR IN CR.NO.165/2022 OF SOLADEVANAHALLI  -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:41471  CRL.P No. 10943 of 2022 POLICE NOW WHICH IS PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE CHIEF JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE AT BENGALURU RURAL DISTRICT,
BENGALURU OFFENCE P/U/S 406,420 R/W 34 OF IPC.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The registration of the FIR for the offences punishable under Sections 406,420,34 of the Indian Penal Code ('the IPC' for short) is impugned by the petitioner- accused No.3.
2.
The respondent No.2 lodged the First Information Report('the FIR' for short).

The summary of the FIR is as follows:
3. Initially, the land bearing survey No.89/1 was granted in favour of one Sri Lakkappa, who is the paternal uncle of the complainant.
The order granting occupancy rights was challenged by one Radhamma before this Court.
The father of the petitioner died in the month of February 1984.
On 26.03.1984, this Court remanded the NC: 2023:KHC:41471 matter to the Land Tribunal for re-consideration of Form No.7 filed in respect of the subject property.
The order of remand, was not brought to the notice of the complainant, and between 1994 to 2002, the complainant sold the land to various persons.
In the year 2015, the Land Tribunal rejected the application for the grant of occupancy rights.
Against the said order, the complainant filed writ petition No.20399/2015 before this Court.

The accused Nos.1 and 2 in the presence of accused No.3 herein induced the complainant to withdraw the petition, stating that they would settle the matter with the purchasers and in lieu of the same would give a sum of Rs.1,00,00,000/- (Rupees One Crore Only).
Believing the said accused, the writ petition was withdrawn.
However, the accused have not paid the amount of Rs.1,00,00,000/- (Rupees One Crore Only) as promised.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that except the allegation that he was present on the date and time when accused Nos.1 and 2 promised the complainant that they would pay a sum of Rs.1,00,00,000/- (Rupees NC: 2023:KHC:41471 One Crore Only)

sentences.text: Therefore, the essential elements to constitute the commission of the offence of cheating is conspicuously absent.

5. Learned HCGP for respondent No.1-State and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that the allegations in the FIR discloses that the commission of the offence of cheating, and the veracity of the allegation requires to be investigated, and at this stage, the registration of FIR does not warrant any interference.
6. Considers the submission made by the learned counsels for the parties.
7.

Except the allegation that the accused herein was present when accused Nos.1 and 2 instructed the complainant to withdraw the petition stating that they would settle the matter with the purchasers and also pay a NC: 2023:KHC:41471 sum of Rs.1,00,00,000/- (Rupees One Crore Only),
there is no allegation that this petitioner either connived with the other accused in inducing the complainant to withdraw the petition.
Therefore, the allegations against the petitioner does not satisfy the essential elements to constitute the commission of offences alleged.
Therefore, the continuation of the investigation would be an abuse process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The criminal petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned FIR in Crime No.165/2022 registered by Soladevanahalli Police Station insofar it relates to petitioner-accused No.3 stands quashed.
